reading_sub: The findings of an investigation, and how carefully they are worded

paras: The vessel lay alongside berth 4, loading iron ore, when she took a list of seven degrees to starboard. Loading was stopped, and the list was corrected over the following four hours by transferring ballast from the starboard tanks to the port side. No cargo was lost and nobody was injured, but the port authority suspended the operation for forty-eight hours.

The stability calculation submitted before loading showed the ship upright at every stage. The investigators concluded that those figures must have been produced from a plan that was never followed: the loading sequence on the manifest called for the two holds nearest the bow to be filled first, and the crane operators had begun amidships. A difference of that size could not have appeared without a change of sequence.

Two other explanations were entertained and discounted. The ballast pumps may have been running against a closed valve, which would have produced a slow list rather than a sudden one. A free surface effect in a partly filled tank could have made the list worse, although it could not have started it. Neither theory accounts for seven degrees in under twenty minutes.

The report notes that the pilot had left the vessel before loading began and that no stage of the loading plan was verified against the manifest at any point. The recommendation is that the officer of the watch confirm each stage against the document before the next hold is opened, and that the keel-to-deck stress figures be recalculated whenever the sequence changes.
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- casualty investigation findings written for this lesson in the register of the PS-ASON reading passages

choices: It explains how iron ore should be loaded on a bulk carrier.
It states one conclusion and shows which other explanations were rejected, and why.
It argues that the port authority was wrong to suspend the operation.

tf: The vessel took a list to starboard while she lay alongside.
The text says she 'lay alongside berth 4, loading iron ore, when she took a list of seven degrees to starboard'.
The stability figures submitted before loading had been fabricated.
The text says the figures 'must have been produced from a plan that was never followed'. That is a different claim: the numbers were real, the plan was not followed.
Trim was restored by shifting ballast from one side to the other.
The text says the list 'was corrected over the following four hours by transferring ballast from the starboard tanks to the port side'.
The investigation discounted free surface effect altogether.
The text says it 'could have made the list worse, although it could not have started it'. It was not ruled out as a factor, only as the cause.
The operation was suspended for forty-eight hours.
The text says 'the port authority suspended the operation for forty-eight hours'.

grammar_question: Three of these are the writer's own conclusions, not things anybody saw. Rank them: which is the surest, which is only possible, and which one is being ruled out?
grammar_rows: near certainty: it is the only explanation left standing
The figures must have been produced from another plan.
one possible explanation among others, not chosen
The pumps may have been running against a closed valve.
it was possible; the report is not saying it happened
Free surface could have made the list worse.
ruled out: the report says it is impossible
It could not have started the list.

must have is the writer's deduction, not a witnessed fact. An option that says 'the text states that the crane operators changed the sequence' is claiming more than the page does -- the page says the writer concluded it.
grammar_insight: A modal perfect is how a report declares its own confidence. In the options, the swap is nearly always between the text STATES and the text SUGGESTS -- and the modal is the only thing on the page that tells you which of the two you are looking at.

prod_sub: Two recordings, then the findings in your own words

listenings.sub: The officer who stopped the loading tells it his way. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: I was on deck when I felt her go over. It was not gradual. One moment we were upright, and inside twenty minutes we had seven degrees to starboard and the gangway was scraping the quay. I stopped the loading straight away and started transferring ballast from the starboard tanks to the port side. That took four hours. Nobody was hurt and we did not lose a single tonne of ore. What I still cannot explain is the plan. The manifest said the two holds nearest the bow first, and I watched the cranes start amidships. Somebody must have changed the sequence, and whoever changed it never told the bridge. The pilot had gone ashore before we opened the first hold, so there was nobody outside the ship to see it either.
questions: How fast did the list develop, and how big was it?
It was not gradual. Inside twenty minutes the vessel had seven degrees to starboard and the gangway was scraping the quay.
What did he do, and how long did it take?
He stopped the loading straight away and transferred ballast from the starboard tanks to the port side. That took four hours.
What is the part he says he cannot explain?
The plan. The manifest called for the two holds nearest the bow first, and the cranes began amidships. He says somebody must have changed the sequence and never told the bridge.

listenings.sub: A pilot describes the passage plan she checks on the way in. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: When I board a ship I am not there to take her over. The master keeps command. What I bring is the water: I know where the bank is, where the current sets, and how the channel behaves on a falling tide. The first thing I ask for is the passage plan. I want to see every waypoint from the pilot station to the berth, with a time against it, and I want to know the draft the ship is leaving with, because that number decides everything else. If a waypoint on the plan does not match what I would do, we discuss it on the bridge before we move, not halfway down the channel. And if the plan has no waypoint for the turn into the basin, we make one. A plan that stops at the harbour entrance is not a plan.
questions: What does the pilot say her job is, and what is it not?
She is not there to take the ship over. The master keeps command. What she brings is knowledge of the water: the bank, the current and how the channel behaves on a falling tide.
What are the two things she asks for first?
The passage plan, with every waypoint from the pilot station to the berth and a time against each one, and the draft the ship is leaving with.
What does she do if a waypoint on the plan does not match what she would do?
They discuss it on the bridge before the ship moves, not halfway down the channel. And if there is no waypoint for the turn into the basin, they make one.

roleplays.label: Guided
roleplays.scenario: Report the incident in five sentences, in this order: where the ship was and what happened, what was done about it, what the investigation concluded, what was ruled out, and what was recommended. Use one modal perfect in sentences three and four.
chips: The investigators concluded that... must have...

roleplays.label: Semi-free
roleplays.scenario: Take the four explanations in the text and rank them out loud, from the one the report is surest about to the one it rules out. For each, say which modal proves your ranking. You may not say the words maybe or probably.

roleplays.label: Free
roleplays.scenario: Read the second paragraph again, then close it. Say two sentences the text STATES and two the text only SUGGESTS, and explain what makes each one what it is. This is the exact distinction the paper builds its wrong options on.
roleplays.note: No support. Target: four sentences, correctly sorted, each with the modal named.

wrap_head: You Can Tell a Finding from a Fact
survival: The vessel lay alongside berth 4 and took a list of seven degrees to starboard.
The list was corrected by transferring ballast from the starboard tanks to the port side.
The investigators concluded that the figures must have been produced from another plan.
A free surface effect could have made the list worse, but it could not have started it.
No stage of the loading plan was verified against the manifest.
checklist: I can name the bow, the stern, starboard and the port side without stopping to think.
I know that port has two meanings and I can tell which one a sentence is using.
I can read must have, may have and could not have and say how sure the writer is.
I can tell a sentence the text STATES from a sentence the text only SUGGESTS.
I can say a set of findings back in my own words, in the right register.

pc_desc: The ten words that name the ship itself and the modal perfects an investigation hedges with. Key words: starboard, port side, bow, stern, keel, ballast, manifest, pilot, berth, waypoint. Structure: modal perfects for deduction about the past.

paras: The investigators concluded that the stability figures must have been produced from a plan that was never followed. A difference of seven degrees could not have appeared without a change of sequence.

Two other explanations were entertained and discounted. The ballast pumps may have been running against a closed valve, which would have produced a slow list rather than a sudden one. A free surface effect in a partly filled tank could have made the list worse, although it could not have started it. Somebody must have changed the loading sequence, and whoever changed it may not have told the bridge.

quiz.q: The figures must have been produced from a plan that was never followed. Did anybody watch that happen?
opts: Yes. Must have reports something a witness saw.
No. Must have is the writer's conclusion: it is the only explanation left standing.
No, and it also means the writer thinks it is unlikely.

quiz.q: Which sentence is the writer LEAST sure about?
opts: A difference of that size could not have appeared without a change of sequence.
The ballast pumps may have been running against a closed valve.
The figures must have been produced from another plan.

quiz.q: It could have made the list worse, although it could not have started it. Is free surface effect ruled out?
opts: Yes, completely. The report discounts it.
Only as the cause. It is still allowed as something that made the list worse.
No. The report says it started the list.

grammar_tip_title: Modal Perfects -- How Sure the Report Is
grammar_tip_lead: A modal perfect is a verb that carries a percentage. It tells you how much of what follows is fact and how much is the writer's own deduction -- and that difference is what the wrong options are built on.

pc_exam_quiz.q: According to the text, it is correct to say that:
opts: trim was restored by shifting ballast from one side of the vessel to the other.
the stability figures submitted before loading had been fabricated.
free surface effect was discounted as a factor altogether.
the pilot was on board throughout the loading operation.
cargo was lost when the vessel took the list.

pc_exam_quiz.q: Mark the option that is NOT true according to the text:
opts: The vessel was moored at her berth when the list developed.
The operation was suspended for two days.
The loading sequence on the manifest began at the bow.
The ballast pumps were found to have been running against a closed valve.
The keel-to-deck stress figures are to be recalculated when the sequence changes.

pc_exam_quiz.q: In the figures must have been produced from a plan that was never followed, the structure shows that the writer is:
opts: reporting what a witness testified.
nearly certain, having ruled the alternatives out.
uncertain and offering one possibility among many.
ruling the explanation out.
quoting the operator's own statement.

pc_exam_quiz.q: In the last paragraph, verified against is closest in meaning to:

copied from

pc_think: Close the text. In about ninety seconds, report the incident as if you were briefing an officer who has to load the same ship tomorrow: what happened, what was concluded, what was ruled out, and what has to change. Use at least three modal perfects and six words from this lesson.

teacher.s1: Abertura (2 min): DECISAO DE DESENHO, valida para todo o programa: TODAS as aulas sao reading-driven, sem alternar com aula de fala (a REGRA 29.2 nao se aplica aqui), porque a prova e 100% leitura. Entre direto, sem cumprimento scriptado (REGRA 27A).
teacher.s2: Homework check + warm-up (5 min): Ela trouxe duas coisas da aula 1: a prova de 2026 anotada e uma lista de dez palavras maritimas que ela ja sabia. Peca a lista. Marque quantas das DEZ de hoje ja estavam la -- esse numero e a linha de base dela e voce vai comparar com ele no fim do bloco. Nao corrija a lista.
teacher.s3: Provocacao (5 min): A frase tem 'port' duas vezes: porto e bombordo. Espere ela achar sozinha. Este e o mecanismo que mais derruba candidato: a palavra e conhecida, o sentido nao. Se ela travar, pergunte: which one can a ship have on one side only?
teacher.s4: Objetivo (2 min): Diga: ten words that name the ship, one verb that says how sure a report is, and the same swap as last week.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: These ten name the ship itself. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (5 min): starboard, port side, bow, stern. NAO traduza (REGRA 13). CCQ: If I am standing on the bridge looking at the bow, is starboard on my right or my left? (Right.) Truque util e classico: port e left tem quatro letras. Peca que ela aponte na tela: bow a frente, stern atras.
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (5 min): keel, ballast, manifest. CCQ para ballast: Is ballast cargo? (No -- water carried for stability, and it is pumped in and out.) CCQ para manifest: Is the manifest a list of the crew? (No -- of what the ship is carrying.) Cuidado com FALSO COGNATO: manifest nao e manifesto de protesto.
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (5 min): pilot, berth, waypoint. CCQ para pilot: Does the pilot take command of the ship? (No -- the master keeps command. Isso volta no listening 2.) CCQ para berth: pergunte os DOIS sentidos (o lugar no cais e o beliche a bordo) -- e outro caso de palavra conhecida no sentido desconhecido.
teacher.s9: Consolidate (4 min): Ela toca a palavra e depois a definicao, LENDO a definicao em voz alta. Se errar, reformule a definicao em vez de dar a resposta.
teacher.s10: Transicao leitura (1 min): Diga: This is the FINDINGS section of a report -- the part where the investigator says what he thinks, and how sure he is. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: a pergunta ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Leitura (7 min): Tres minutos em silencio, sem dicionario. NAO traduza. Se ela parar numa palavra, pergunte What do you think it means, from the sentence? Depois peca UMA frase de resumo. O detalhe fica para o true/false.
teacher.s12: Gist (3 min): Ela escolhe e JUSTIFICA (Why not a? Why not c?). A opcao (a) e a armadilha classica: e sobre o mesmo assunto e nao e o que o texto faz.
teacher.s13: True or False (7 min): REGRA DA CASA: ela diz TRUE ou FALSE e DEPOIS LE EM VOZ ALTA a linha que prova. As afirmacoes 2 e 4 sao as importantes -- as duas mudam a FORCA da afirmacao do texto sem mudar o assunto, e e assim que a prova monta distrator.
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: You just read four conclusions and none of them is a fact. Let us see how the writer told you that.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (7 min): Nao de a regra. Peca que ela RANQUEIE os quatro exemplos por certeza. So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ decisivo: If the option says 'the text states that the operators changed the sequence', is that right? (No -- the text says the writer CONCLUDED it.) Ela estuda gramatica sozinha: aqui a gramatica so serve como ferramenta de leitura, nao peca producao.
teacher.s16: Practice (4 min): Ela diz a forma ORALMENTE antes de clicar. Se travar, pergunte: sure, possible, or ruled out?
teacher.s17: Spot the error (4 min): Os quatro sao os erros classicos de modal perfect: must been (falta o have), may have ran (participio errado), could not have start (participio errado), must had (had no lugar de have).
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Same four findings, other words. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (4 min): Os quatro pares saiam do texto que ela acabou de ler. Pergunte, para cada par: which of the two is on the page? Ela vai ver que a direita nunca esta.
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (5 min): Ela toca a frase de registro alto e depois o que aquilo diz em ingles simples. Depois cubra a coluna da direita e faca a direcao dificil: dada a frase simples, como a prova escreveria?
teacher.s21: Complete (5 min): Teacher-led. Leia em voz alta e pare em cada lacuna; ela escolhe do banco. As oito respostas sao as dez palavras da aula -- se ela hesitar, releia a frase inteira.
teacher.s22: Quick fire (6 min): Uma pergunta por vez, EM VOZ ALTA, antes das dicas. Meta: menos de dez segundos por pergunta. A ultima (bow, stern, starboard, port side em ordem) tem de sair sem pensar.
teacher.s23: Transicao (1 min): Diga: The same incident, told by the man who was standing on the deck. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening 1 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Escuta dela foi medida em 0%: comece em 0.75x sem perguntar. Toque duas vezes, sem texto. Depois pergunte: he says somebody MUST HAVE changed the sequence -- is that the same thing the written report says? (E sim: e a mesma deducao, no mesmo modal.)
teacher.s25: Listening 2 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Este audio interessa a ela por dois motivos: traz waypoint e pilot vivos, e descreve a funcao que ela quer exercer. Pergunte no fim: what surprised you about what the pilot does NOT do?
teacher.s26: Role-play guiado (4 min): Cinco frases com os frames. NAO corrija durante. Conte quantos modal perfects CORRETOS ela produz e diga o numero no fim.
teacher.s27: Role-play semi-livre (5 min): Proibir maybe e probably e o exercicio inteiro: sem eles ela tem de usar o modal. Se ela escorregar, aponte com o dedo e espere.
teacher.s28: Producao livre (6 min): O que voce esta medindo e se ela separa STATES de SUGGESTS e nomeia o modal que prova. Nao interrompa. Reformule depois, sem apontar erro.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Let us see what you can do now.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): Cinco frases do proprio texto. Toque e peca repeticao. Insista em starboard (pronuncia STAR-berd, nao star-BOARD) e keel.
teacher.s31: Checklist (2 min): Leia cada item em voz alta. Os 5 checks fecham a aula e acendem o stamp.
teacher.s32: Encerramento (2 min): Diga: Lesson 2 complete, Helena. HOMEWORK ORALMENTE, nunca escrito na tela: (1) responder as questoes de ingles da prova de 2026 que ela ainda nao respondeu, sem dicionario, e anotar em duas frases qual foi a mais dificil e por que; (2) montar um deck de dez cards com as palavras de hoje -- palavra na frente, definicao em ingles e uma frase de contexto naval atras. Proxima aula: Rules of the Sea.
